newsitem.title: USA: Congoleum sees Q2 sales, income down.
newsitem.headline: Congoleum sees Q2 sales, income down.

text.p: Congoleum Corp said Tuesday that it anticipates second quarter 1997 sales and income will be "substantially" below the levels of the second quarter of 1996, but higher than in the first quarter of 1997.

The company attributed second quarter results to problems related to its shutdown and refurbishment at its Marcus Hook facility and said sales were hurt by lower demand for products in both the manufactured housing and general retail segments.
Congoleum earned $4.9 million, or $0.48 a share on sales of $74.4 million in the second quarter of 1996, and $1.0 million, or $0.10 a share on sales of $61.1 million in the first quarter of 1997.
The company said that it was not able to manufacture normal levels of special run, promotional products to provide incremental sales and profit during the second quarter, due to the shutdown.

Congoleom also refrained from its customary level of consumer promotions to assure an adequate inventory build and devoted more capacity than planned for expanding sales in the do-it-yourself category, it said.

The company said it expects the balance of the year to benefit from sales of a new product being introduced in the third quarter, its upcoming sales initiatives in the do-it-yourself category, and a resumption of its normal promotional and consumer marketing activities.
It said it is also beginning to see indications of potentially lower raw material costs going forward.
Congoleum is 44 percent owned by American Biltrite Inc.
